headline: SpaceX struggles. Serbia joins. True Anomaly raises.
deck: This week saw SpaceX's launch woes and Serbia's geopolitical pivot, while True Anomaly secured significant funding.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M Series C amid defense demand
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in a Series C funding round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The company focuses on co-orbital security and space domain awareness, tapping into the Department of Defense's growing appetite for advanced space technologies. Their latest round underscores the increasing importance of space security in national defense strategies.
stories.soWhat: It's clear that in the current climate, cash is king, especially when it comes to defense-related ventures.

stories.head: Serbia signs Artemis Accords, snubbing China
stories.body: Serbia officially joined the Artemis Accords this week, aligning itself with U.S. lunar exploration efforts after previously considering ties with China's lunar ambitions. This geopolitical shift highlights the delicate balance countries maintain when choosing sides in the space race, particularly as they navigate economic and security interests.
stories.soWhat: Serbia's pivot to the U.S. is a reminder that in space, allegiances can shift faster than a rocket launch countdown.

stories.head: SpaceX's Starship Flight 13 launch aborted again
stories.body: SpaceX's Starship Flight 13 was aborted due to engine issues, marking yet another setback for the ambitious program. This incident follows a series of hiccups in the Starship development timeline, raising questions about the reliability of the vehicle as SpaceX prepares for its IPO. Investors are watching closely as the company aims to solidify its position in the market.
stories.soWhat: If SpaceX can't get its flagship rocket off the ground, its IPO might just be a high-stakes gamble.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on SpaceX's next launch attempt
watchlist.body: The outcome of the next Starship launch will be critical for investor confidence and future funding.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser moves closer to flight

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension implications
watchlist.body: The $480 million extension for the TITAN ground station may signal increased government reliance on commercial data solutions.

watchlist.title: Watch for more defense-tech IPOs
watchlist.body: As the defense-tech IPO window opens, expect a flurry of activity as startups seek to capitalize on heightened interest.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
